levels.definition: A defect can destroy or disclose user data, violate a mandatory legal or security boundary, or make a critical workflow inaccessible without a safe workaround.
A defect materially breaks media correctness, real-time continuity, or a primary workflow and has no complete recovery path.
A defect has bounded impact and a documented workaround, but remains visible in a supported workflow.
A defect is cosmetic or low impact and does not compromise correctness, access, security, licensing, or recovery.

defectClasses.releaseCondition: All destructive and migratory paths preserve the last recoverable revision and pass format-specific round-trip and failure-injection tests.
defectClasses.escalation: Stop distribution, preserve affected artifacts, identify the last safe build, and begin rollback and recovery immediately.

defectClasses.releaseCondition: Every applicable named fixture remains within its committed synchronization budget on each qualified platform tier.
defectClasses.escalation: Classify as critical when rendered output cannot be recovered from the project source; otherwise block the affected tier until requalified.

defectClasses.releaseCondition: Recording, playback, monitoring, and render fixtures report no unexplained dropout beyond their committed quality budgets.
defectClasses.escalation: Classify as critical when captured input is silently lost or overwritten; otherwise block the affected audio path and platform tier.

defectClasses.releaseCondition: Preview and export frame loss remains within the fixture-specific budget and every loss is surfaced by telemetry or an explicit error.
defectClasses.escalation: Classify as critical when the exported artifact is silently incomplete or source state is damaged; otherwise block the affected video path.

defectClasses.releaseCondition: Every primary workflow is keyboard operable, labelled, focus safe, and usable at the supported zoom and contrast settings on the qualified browser and desktop matrix.
defectClasses.escalation: Block the affected product and tier; require an accessibility owner to approve the corrected qualification evidence.

defectClasses.releaseCondition: All enabled input, renderer, IPC, filesystem, helper, and extension boundaries have passing negative tests and no unresolved release-blocked risk.
defectClasses.escalation: Stop distribution, rotate or revoke affected material where applicable, preserve evidence, and follow the security response procedure before requalification.

defectClasses.releaseCondition: Every distributed component has verified source, license, notice, rebuild, and delivery evidence required by its distribution surface.
defectClasses.escalation: Stop publishing the affected artifact, retain the release manifest, and require provenance and licensing review before rebuilding.
